issue.title: test_shell_done_marker_writers_stamp_finished_at_through_shared_helper: src/sase/monitor/start.py no longer writes a shell done marker
issue.description:
tests/shells/test_shells_substrate.py::test_shell_done_marker_writers_stamp_finished_at_through_shared_helper fails on master c12285ffd4 (confirmed reproducible on a clean git stash with no working-tree changes, so this predates and is unrelated to my in-progress src/sase/monitor/store.py split work).

The test scans src/sase/monitor/*.py and src/sase/gate_shell/*.py for files that call write_done_marker_and_update_index(, and asserts a hardcoded frozenset _KNOWN_SHELL_DONE_WRITERS is a subset of what it found. src/sase/monitor/start.py is in that hardcoded set, but grep confirms start.py's current source contains no write_done_marker_and_update_index( call at all -- only src/sase/monitor/reconcile.py, start_runtime.py, supervise.py, resume_delivery_state.py, and proc_adapter.py call it.

Likely root cause: some prior monitor refactor (e.g. the sase-kp epic or a later toobig split) moved the done-marker write that used to live directly in start.py out into one of those other files, and _KNOWN_SHELL_DONE_WRITERS in tests/shells/test_shells_substrate.py was never updated to drop start.py. Fix is likely just removing 'src/sase/monitor/start.py' from _KNOWN_SHELL_DONE_WRITERS (after confirming start.py never wrote the marker directly, or that responsibility moved to one of the still-listed files), but a worker should verify with git blame/log on both the marker-write call sites and the test's known-writer set before changing it.

Reproduce: uv run python -m pytest tests/shells/test_shells_substrate.py::test_shell_done_marker_writers_stamp_finished_at_through_shared_helper -q

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic static-source-scan assertion, not a runtime race: it greps for a literal call string across a fixed set of files and compares against a hardcoded frozenset. Reproduced identically on repeated runs and on a clean git stash of master with zero working-tree changes.
